$doc: THE FE↔BE WIRE CONTRACT — strings that must be byte-identical in
Easyfix_CRM_UI and EasyFix_Backend because they cross the network or land
in a shared database column. A type-checker cannot see across the two
repos, so these are the values that drift silently and fail in production.
THIS FILE IS DUPLICATED, BYTE FOR BYTE, IN BOTH REPOS AT shared/wire-contract.json.
To change anything here: edit BOTH copies in the same change and run
`npm test` in BOTH repos. Each repo's tests/wire-contract.test.js asserts
its own constants against its own copy, and — when the sibling repo is
checked out beside it, which is the normal dev layout — asserts the two
copies are identical.
WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT GUARANTEE. In CI each repo can only see itself,
so CI catches the common failure: someone edits a constant in code and
forgets this file. It cannot catch a self-consistent edit made to one repo
alone — that is caught locally, where both repos are checked out.
tbl_job.time_slot — the BROAD booking band. EXACTLY these four values.
Spelling is deliberate: no spaces around the hour tokens, the word 'to'
as the separator, NOT an en-dash. Do not tidy them.
Windows are half-open [fromHour, toHour). 'After Hours' is everything
outside them and has no derivable window, hence null.
Values the FE sends as ?sortBy= on GET /admin/jobs. Each MUST be a key of
SORTABLE_COLUMNS in EasyFix_Backend/services/job.service.js, because the
list validator derives its allow-list from those keys — an unknown literal
is not a silent no-op, Joi rejects it and the whole page 400s.
This shipped once as 'ageSecs' (the projection alias) and blanked the jobs
grid for anyone who had ?sort=ageSecs:asc persisted in a bookmarked URL.
